slides.title: Me-facts point at you
slides.text: Pim says some facts are me-facts. Your name, your school, where you live and your birthday are all me-facts. Together, they can point straight at you.
slides.alt: A letter from Birthday Club with both clues marked: three me-facts asked together, and a surprise present as the bait.

focus.cue: Name, birthday and address, asked together

slides.title: Sort the postcards
slides.text: Pim sorts her postcards into two trays. Fun facts go in the Share tray. Me-facts go in the Keep Private tray.
steps: Keep private: a photo in school uniform
slides.alt: Lock It, the sharing sort: the first card, where you live, waits for its tray. Share, or keep it private?

focus.cue: The first card to sort: where you live
Share, or keep private? Every card gets a tray

slides.title: Small facts can join up
slides.text: One fact alone may look harmless. Add two more, and the three together can point at one child. That is why me-facts stay private online.
slides.alt: A post from Name Maker with both clues marked: “Your first pet’s name plus your street name” and “tag five friends”.

focus.cue: Two small facts, joined into one big clue
Tagging five friends spreads the trick

slides.title: Games do not need me-facts
slides.text: Some games and sites ask for me-facts before you can play. A real game never needs your address to let you play. If a game asks, stop and tell a trusted adult.
slides.alt: A card from “A new friend”, marked unknown sender, asking to get together after school. Cues to tap: a personal question, from someone you have never met.

focus.cue: Someone from the game asks for your street
A real game never needs to know where you live

words.means: only for you and the trusted adults who look after you
facts about you, like your name, school or birthday
to show or give something to other people
something that is true about a person or a thing

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Private Facts and sort all 6 messages. For each one, ask: could this point at me? Then choose a move.
slides.alt: A game chat from MapGamePal with both clues marked: “Which school do you go to?” and “what street do you walk home on?”

focus.cue: Play Private Facts: could this point at me?
